description: Fortinet, Inc. provides cybersecurity and convergence of networking and security solutions worldwide. The company offers FortiOS, a unified operating system designed to address cybersecurity threats;
description_full: Fortinet, Inc. provides cybersecurity and convergence of networking and security solutions worldwide. The company offers FortiOS, a unified operating system designed to address cybersecurity threats; FortiASIC application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC)-based security processing units; FortiCloud, a private cloud software as a service platform; FortiAI, which provides a dual-layered defense across the Fortinet Security Fabric; FortiEndpoint, which converges secure connectivity, endpoint protection, and capabilities into a single agent; and OT Security, which protect the engineered systems that underpin infrastructure and supply chains. It also provides secure networking solutions that focus on the convergence of networking and security; network firewall solutions comprising FortiGate data centers, hyperscale, and distributed firewalls; wireless local area network solutions; and secure connectivity solutions. In addition, the company offers the Fortinet Unified Secure Access Service Edge solutions that include firewall, software-defined wide-area network, secure web gateway, cloud access services broker, data loss prevention, and zero trust network access; and web application firewalls, cloud network security with virtualized firewalls, cloud-native firewalls, cloud-native application protection, and code security. Further, it provides AI-driven security operation solutions, which include a suite of cybersecurity solutions, as well as FortiEDR, FortiXDR, FortiNDR, FortiSandbox, FortiDeceptor, FortiDLP, and FortiRecon. Additionally, the company offers FortiGuard Labs, a cybersecurity threat intelligence and research organization; FortiGuard and Other Security Services, a suite of AI-powered security capabilities that consists of FortiGuard application, content, device, NOC/SOC, and web security services; and FortiCare technical support services. Fortinet, Inc. was incorporated in 2000 and is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California.

financial_summary: Fortinet, Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $93.5B market cap on $6.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years and +21% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 66% against a 11% cost of capital — a 55-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 75% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $2.2B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.40× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 17% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 31% operating margin runs 24pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.31x).
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+12.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 135% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 22% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 35% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 49% and a beta of 1.24, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $651.7M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 38% in the 2020 crash and 34% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $79.69 (margin of safety -60%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 2%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $56.29 to $116 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 41.6 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 33.0 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 42.0 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 6% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The 37 covering analysts target $145 on average, 14% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 66% clears the cost of capital of 10.6% by 55pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.61).
It runs a 75% gross margin and converts 33% of revenue into free cash flow, or 29% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.40x.
ROE of 150% is amplified by 8.4x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 12pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 12.0% of revenue on R&D and 4.1% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.5B (2% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.5, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 137 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.5% over 3 years, 21.3% over 5 years and 21.0% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 18.4% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.11 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 1.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 12%.
Capex runs 2.4x depreciation (5.4% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
Its Rule of 40 score is 50, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 17.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 71%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (29 sales, net $57.5M sold).
It returns 2.4% a year to shareholders (2.4% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 1.9% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 15,540 employees, each generates about $438K of revenue, 1.2x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 21.6% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $143K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
CEO pay is $1.3M (3x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
